verdicts.task2_script_catchability: A pure existence script (extract every symbol, check it exists) would catch NONE of the 19 - every named symbol in the 19 wrong claims exists; the errors are in what the docs say the symbols do. Stronger mechanical checks (quoted-string grep, counts, arithmetic, cross-document citation checks, absence-claim grep, staleness) would catch 7 of 19: #4 counterexample scan (7 modules > 2), #6 quoted-string grep ('rikta kosh se' 0 hits), #9 internal arithmetic (16+8192=8208, not 8272), #12 count check (331/347, neither 344), #13 provenance grep (16385 appears 0 times in the R148 report), #14 staleness (header pins v300, tree is v315), #19 absence-claim grep (munmap exists at r65_arena.inc:713). 12 of 19 need a human reader: order of checks (#5), dead vs live code (#16), reasons (#10), closure arguments, runtime behaviour, measurements, paraphrase fidelity, historical claims (#17, #18, #1, #2, #3, #7, #8, #11, #15). Recommendation: build the script for the mechanical classes as a FAIL-on-drift gate (like check_doc_signatures.py), not a review list (like doc_stale_claims.py); it is a floor, not a proof.
